key_insight: LADRC improved current-regulation robustness in a fast-frequency pulsed welding power supply, but was not faster than PI at every operating point.
engineering_relevance: More consistent current response under changing load and dc-bus conditions could support reliable pulsed welding power delivery.
method: Modeled load-dependent damping, commutation duty loss, and ADC/PWM scaling in a dual-path PSFB supply.
Implemented a first-order LADRC regulator with a second-order observer on an STM32G474 at a 20-μs control period.
Compared hardware performance against locally gain-scanned incremental PI control.
evidence_signal: Hardware tests showed mean rise-time drift of 15.7% versus 56.0% for PI across 544–420 V bus levels, 45.5% lower mean pulse recovery time, and amplitude variation falling from 4.13% to 1.28% at 50 A.
watch_item: Results establish application-specific electrical gains, not parameter-independent dynamics or validated improvements in weld quality.
paper_title: Study on Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control for Current Regulation in a Fast‐Frequency Pulsed Welding Power Supply
